result.title: The Last Remote Sensing Model Built by Humans? Casting Any Earth Observation Task as Recursive Self-Improvement
result.summary: Earth observation (EO) models are still built by hand. For each new task, experts design a training recipe and tune it against a benchmark. We show that this loop can be handed to an agent. Any verifiable task can be cast as a harness and a verifier, where the harness defines what the agent may use and the verifier defines what counts as success. Every EO task can be made verifiable, through labeled benchmarks, independent sensors, physical models or the repeated observation of the same place. Given only these two components, a general-purpose coding agent builds the EO model and improves it recursively on its own outputs. Settings long treated as separate research problems, from learning with a handful of labels to adapting across domains, become choices of harness and verifier. On four EO benchmarks spanning optical, SAR and multispectral time-series imagery, agent-built models surpass the state of the art and keep most of that accuracy from about 1% of the training labels. This establishes a new paradigm for EO, in which people design harnesses and verifiers and agents build the models, so EO models improve as agents do.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将任意可验证的地球观测任务表述为「harness + verifier」，让通用编码智能体自行构建并递归改进 EO 模型，在光学、SAR 与多光谱基准上以约 1% 标签取得超越 SOTA 的精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「可验证任务 + 递归自改进」的设定，可能为 LVR 中推理轨迹的监督、验证与自改进训练提供可核查的方法线索；但研究对象是遥感模型构建，本身不涉及视觉 latent 状态。
